content:
[原文] With the rapid rise in the number of Mac AI agents requesting "full disk access," Apple says it will adjust macOS to protect user privacy.

[原文] Although Apple has not yet revealed specific details, the company says users should understand what it really means to grant such "very high" permissions to applications.

[原文] In a blog post on its Developer website, Apple explained that the full disk access feature in macOS was originally designed to "let backup apps work properly on Mac." However, Apple pointed out that "some developers" are using the full disk access setting in macOS in ways that could put users at risk.

[原文] Apple responded by saying it will "introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant such extremely high permissions to applications must do so through very explicit user actions."

[原文] The company did not elaborate further on these controls or the planned changes. Nonetheless, Apple said the rise of "increasingly capable and autonomous" AI agents is drawing greater attention to privacy and security needs:

[原文] Apple's announcement comes at a time when tools such as Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots are gaining popularity. These always-on AI agents request access to large amounts of users' personal data, and we have already seen some negative cases involving Meta Muse.
